npcs.name: Ilsa Riverglass
npcs.description: An envoy seeking a workable border agreement while questioning the mandate her own superiors gave her.
npcs.appearance: Travel-worn blue silk, a plain pin representing her office and a case of carefully sorted correspondence.
npcs.personality: Poised, curious and guarded; advocates listening while withholding the parts of her position she doubts.

speech.manner: Restates an opposing concern before answering.
speech.exampleLine: Before we agree on a border, whom are we asking to live with it?

npcs.background: Spent years translating disputes between settlements. Her first major appointment has a deadline incompatible with meaningful consultation.

motivations.desire: Reach an agreement residents can live with.
motivations.fear: Being praised for an accord that harms people absent from the room.

offer.provides: Official introductions, negotiation context and access to public proposals.
offer.wantsInReturn: Accurate messages and consent before attributing statements.

relationships: A superior wants quick signatures.
A local organizer asks for time to consult residents.

secret.truth: She has authority to extend the talks but has not disclosed it.
clues: Her commission includes an unused extension clause.
A secretary has reserved rooms beyond the public deadline.
discoveryPaths: Read the published terms of her commission.
Ask the secretary why the extra rooms were booked.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She asks an overlooked attendant how the proposed change affects their road home.

socialResponses.respect: Shares the limits and flexibility of her mandate.
socialResponses.pressure: Sticks to documented positions and consults affected people.
socialResponses.betrayal: Corrects misattributed statements and suspends informal talks.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Request a public extension with stated reasons.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Diplomacy creates options; she cannot promise acceptance by either side.

npcs.name: Ereth Cinderhall
npcs.description: An heir more interested in useful craft than courtly display, unsure how to turn personal refusal into responsible leadership.
npcs.appearance: Dark red scales, understated formal clothes and callused fingers poorly hidden by gloves.
npcs.personality: Earnest, awkward and resistant to ceremony; mistakes rejecting privilege for understanding everyone else's burdens.

speech.manner: Plain speech punctuated by apologies for inherited conventions.
speech.exampleLine: I can refuse the chair. That does not mend what is broken beneath it.

npcs.background: Learned woodworking during years away from the household. Returned when a parent's illness made succession an immediate responsibility.

motivations.desire: Give estate workers a real voice in its management.
motivations.fear: Turning a fashionable reform into another family performance.

offer.provides: Household introductions, craft contacts and a willing listener in the succession dispute.
offer.wantsInReturn: Specific proposals and honesty about their costs.

relationships: A parent fears loss of family authority.
A workshop mentor refuses to become a decorative adviser.

secret.truth: Ereth intends to share succession responsibilities with an overlooked sibling.
clues: Private correspondence discusses joint signatures.
A new office contains two matching desks.
discoveryPaths: Ask the sibling about their plans.
Discuss governance terms with both of them.

narratorNotes.firstScene: Ereth repairs a broken stool while a herald waits to announce them.

socialResponses.respect: Accepts correction and credits other people's expertise.
socialResponses.pressure: Retreats into stubborn refusal before reconsidering.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends personal sponsorship but considers the proposal independently.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Invite the sibling and workers to draft a management charter.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Do not make good intentions instant legitimacy; affected people may reasonably distrust the reform.

npcs.name: Baron Soon
npcs.role: Noble whose grand opening never happens
npcs.description: A baron who continually postpones a magnificent public opening because admitting that the building is modest feels unbearable.
npcs.appearance: A dazzling sash over dusty boots, curls combed for a ceremony and scissors kept in a velvet presentation box.
npcs.personality: Affable, vain and anxious; generous with visions, unreliable with decisions.

speech.manner: Speaks of imminent splendor in increasingly vague dates.
speech.exampleLine: Soon is not a date. It is a commitment to possibility.

npcs.background: Promised a grand civic hall, then discovered the budget supported only a useful small one. Keeps commissioning new ceremonial plans.

motivations.desire: Be celebrated for something the town can actually use.
motivations.fear: Opening a building that exposes his ordinary means.

offer.provides: Patron introductions, event contacts and access to unfinished public works.
offer.wantsInReturn: Help make a modest result feel dignified.

relationships: A builder wants a final decision.
A school committee needs the usable rooms immediately.

secret.truth: Several rooms are finished and quietly host lessons already.
clues: Fresh chalk appears behind ceremonial drapes.
The caretaker's timetable names daily classes.
discoveryPaths: Ask the caretaker who uses the rooms.
Attend a lesson with the committee's permission.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He rehearses cutting a ribbon stretched across a closed storeroom.

socialResponses.respect: Allows others to simplify the ceremony.
socialResponses.pressure: Announces another postponement, then seeks private reassurance.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws honorary invitations while protecting the project's reputation.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Visit the classes and consider opening only the finished rooms.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: The building is real; grandeur is his avoidance strategy, not an endless random gag.

npcs.name: Lady Crumbcourt
npcs.role: Self-appointed aristocrat of the public square
npcs.description: A talking pigeon who presides over a grand court of overlooked square-dwellers and wants its community treated with respect.
npcs.appearance: A tiny brocade collar, one iridescent feather arranged like a crest and a cushion on a statue's shoulder.
npcs.personality: Proud, attentive and territorial; considers her petitioners family but occasionally confuses caretaking with ownership.

speech.manner: Lavish titles followed by concise complaints.
speech.exampleLine: The square requests an audience. Preferably one with crumbs.

npcs.background: Speech made her a local curiosity. She organized people and animals who relied on the square into a playful but useful mutual-aid court.

motivations.desire: Keep the square accessible during a redevelopment scheme.
motivations.fear: Being displayed as a mascot while her community is displaced.

offer.provides: Local observations, introductions and an organized circle of residents.
offer.wantsInReturn: Hear petitioners directly and offer practical support.

relationships: A street cleaner is her trusted chamberlain.
A developer offers an ornamental aviary.

secret.truth: She has privately considered the aviary to guarantee her own comfort.
clues: She asks unusually detailed questions about its cushions.
A proposal copy carries her small claw marks.
discoveryPaths: Discuss the offer with the street cleaner.
Ask who would still be allowed inside the square.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She announces a hearing about a moved bench with enormous dignity.

socialResponses.respect: Shares the floor with real residents.
socialResponses.pressure: Calls witnesses and refuses private assurances.
socialResponses.betrayal: Publicly removes a court title and explains the breach.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Invite residents to inspect the redevelopment proposal.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her court conveys community needs; she has no automatic authority over people or birds.

npcs.name: Halden Rook
npcs.description: A watch sergeant who knows his district intimately and has grown too willing to decide which rules deserve enforcement.
npcs.appearance: A weathered blue coat, carefully polished badge and a tired face that brightens when neighbors greet him.
npcs.personality: Patient, protective and paternalistic; calls his exceptions fair without asking everyone affected.

speech.manner: Specific names and places; dislikes vague accusations.
speech.exampleLine: Tell me where it happened. Then tell me who had to clean it up.

npcs.background: Has served the same district for years. Familiarity made him useful and slowly insulated him from scrutiny.

motivations.desire: Keep the district stable through a contentious change in leadership.
motivations.fear: An outsider exposing his favors without understanding their context.

offer.provides: Public incident records, local introductions and procedural guidance.
offer.wantsInReturn: Clear accounts and respect for complainants' privacy.

relationships: A shopkeeper depends on his informal mediation.
A new supervisor demands consistent reporting.

secret.truth: He omitted a well-connected neighbor's complaint from the official record.
clues: The complainant's receipt has no matching entry.
His notebook contains an appointment absent from the watch log.
discoveryPaths: Compare the receipt with public records.
Hear the complainant's account of the meeting.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He stops to ask a vendor whether an earlier problem was actually resolved.

socialResponses.respect: Explains procedures and can admit an exception.
socialResponses.pressure: Demands a specific allegation and documented evidence.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends informal cooperation and submits his own account.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Reopen the omitted complaint before the supervisor finds it.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Present civic authority through relationships and process; do not infer combat abilities from the role.

npcs.name: Ema Fairline
npcs.description: A registrar simplifying public paperwork while quietly resisting demands for lists of vulnerable residents.
npcs.appearance: Tidy dark braids, green sleeves protected by cuffs and a desk free of decorative objects.
npcs.personality: Exact, stubborn and unexpectedly kind; believes clarity solves more problems than it actually does.

speech.manner: Explains one requirement at a time.
speech.exampleLine: You need proof of residence. You do not owe me your whole story.

npcs.background: Entered the office after her family spent months correcting a name error. She now pushes for accessible records and limited collection.

motivations.desire: Replace arbitrary procedures with plain public rules.
motivations.fear: Her accurate records becoming a tool for exclusion.

offer.provides: Document context, public records and introductions to civic offices.
offer.wantsInReturn: Consent for personal disclosures and accurate submitted information.

relationships: A senior official requests detailed resident lists.
A neighborhood advocate brings difficult cases.

secret.truth: She has delayed a discriminatory list by documenting minor errors one at a time.
clues: Requests repeatedly return with unusually detailed corrections.
A clerk keeps a separate calendar of those delays.
discoveryPaths: Compare the request dates.
Ask Ema why these corrections receive special attention.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She rewrites an official instruction in ordinary language for a visitor.

socialResponses.respect: Finds lawful alternatives and explains limits.
socialResponses.pressure: Insists requests be recorded and signed.
socialResponses.betrayal: Revokes private assistance and informs affected applicants.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Submit a formal challenge to the list request.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: She can interpret procedures, not create identities or waive every requirement.

npcs.name: Sovan Plainstone
npcs.description: A magistrate known for calm hearings who fears that a reputation for decisiveness is pushing him to conceal uncertainty.
npcs.appearance: A dark robe with a worn collar, square reading glasses and hands folded tightly when listening.
npcs.personality: Serious, patient and status-conscious; values fair hearings but dislikes admitting he needs help.

speech.manner: Restates claims without adopting either speaker's certainty.
speech.exampleLine: Let us separate what happened from what each of you believes it means.

npcs.background: Worked as a neighborhood mediator before appointment. Formal authority brought unfamiliar disputes and pressure to produce clear answers quickly.

motivations.desire: Establish a transparent record of how decisions are reached.
motivations.fear: A disputed decision defining his entire public career.

offer.provides: Hearing context, published decisions and mediator introductions.
offer.wantsInReturn: Specific testimony and willingness to hear other accounts.

relationships: A clerk notices contradictions he overlooks.
A patron expects gratitude for supporting his appointment.

secret.truth: He relied on the patron's unsupported recommendation in an earlier property decision.
clues: The published explanation cites a missing survey.
The clerk's notes record the patron's private visit.
discoveryPaths: Compare the cited documents.
Ask the affected residents how the hearing was conducted.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He asks a clerk to read an overlooked sentence aloud.

socialResponses.respect: Allows correction and explains his reasoning.
socialResponses.pressure: Adjourns discussion instead of inventing certainty.
socialResponses.betrayal: Records the broken terms and uses formal channels.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Review the earlier decision with independent advice.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: His judgments are local institutions' acts, not unquestionable moral truth.

npcs.name: Vessa Cointurn
npcs.description: An ambitious assessor determined to make powerful households pay fairly, yet tempted to protect her own advancement.
npcs.appearance: A sharply cut coat, short dark curls and a leather case with color-coded property maps.
npcs.personality: Energetic, skeptical and competitive; notices evasions quickly but interprets disagreement as obstruction.

speech.manner: Concise comparisons between claims and visible facts.
speech.exampleLine: If the storehouse is empty, why are its deliveries on the street?

npcs.background: Started assessing market stalls, then uncovered inconsistent treatment of larger estates. Her next promotion depends on handling that discovery quietly.

motivations.desire: Publish a consistent assessment process.
motivations.fear: Losing influence before she can make the process stick.

offer.provides: Public valuation records, ownership context and civic introductions.
offer.wantsInReturn: Verifiable details rather than rumors or personal favors.

relationships: A market association supports her reform.
A superior wants one estate left unexamined.

secret.truth: She delayed examining that estate in exchange for a promised promotion.
clues: A scheduled visit disappears from the calendar.
The promotion letter arrived the same week.
discoveryPaths: Compare the public inspection schedule.
Ask the association why its petition stopped advancing.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She checks a grand gate against a surprisingly modest declaration.

socialResponses.respect: Shows her method and accepts contrary evidence.
socialResponses.pressure: Narrows discussion to documents and witnesses.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends private cooperation and discloses relevant arrangements.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Schedule the delayed visit publicly.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her scrutiny can be useful and intrusive; give ordinary residents valid concerns about it.

npcs.name: Inspector Sideways
npcs.description: A civic inspector who treats awkward architecture as an interpersonal grievance and writes complaints on behalf of neglected stairs.
npcs.appearance: A slanted hat, perfectly straight tie and measuring tools arranged in a case shaped like a crooked doorway.
npcs.personality: Observant, earnest and officious; identifies real inconveniences but imagines every structure wants his personal attention.

speech.manner: Addresses buildings politely, then translates their supposed concerns.
speech.exampleLine: This staircase feels overlooked. Also, its third step is loose.

npcs.background: Started investigating poorly maintained public buildings. A theatrical persona made reports memorable and now threatens to overshadow practical findings.

motivations.desire: Make basic maintenance impossible to ignore.
motivations.fear: Being dismissed as entertainment while dangerous neglect continues.

offer.provides: Maintenance records, caretaker introductions and practical observations.
offer.wantsInReturn: Allow inspection and respond to the actual repair issue.

relationships: A carpenter respects his useful reports.
A mayor invites him to festivals but ignores his recommendations.

secret.truth: He invented a dramatic complaint to force attention to a routine repair.
clues: His initial report is far less theatrical.
The caretaker remembers supplying the exact wording.
discoveryPaths: Compare versions of the report.
Ask the caretaker what repair remains undone.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He apologizes to a bench before checking its supports.

socialResponses.respect: Shows the real issue beneath the performance.
socialResponses.pressure: Requests a written response and becomes painfully formal.
socialResponses.betrayal: Publishes accurate findings without the private conversation.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Present one plain report without speaking for the furniture.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Buildings need not literally speak; distinguish his personification from established magic.

npcs.name: Magistrate Hush
npcs.description: A slow-speaking mediator who schedules elaborate hearings for noise complaints while suspecting silence is not always peace.
npcs.appearance: A dark shawl over a carefully polished shell and a tiny wooden sign reading Please Finish Your Thought.
npcs.personality: Patient, exact and quietly mischievous; enjoys order but sometimes prolongs proceedings to avoid making a choice.

speech.manner: Long pauses, then devastatingly ordinary questions.
speech.exampleLine: At what point did the rooster become a political statement?

npcs.background: Was asked to settle a dispute over bells and became the town's specialist in awkward neighbor conflicts.

motivations.desire: Create agreements people keep after leaving the room.
motivations.fear: A tidy ruling merely hiding a deeper grievance.

offer.provides: Mediation, neighborhood context and public complaint records.
offer.wantsInReturn: Each side must describe a practical change it could accept.

relationships: A bell keeper fears losing a tradition.
A sleepless baker wants one quiet morning.

secret.truth: He has postponed the bell ruling because he personally likes the ceremony.
clues: His window overlooks the bell tower.
The postponed draft favors its keeper.
discoveryPaths: Ask how he experienced the bell before taking the case.
Read the draft with both parties present.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He opens a hearing by asking whether the complaint has changed since breakfast.

socialResponses.respect: Allows a workable compromise to replace his favorite answer.
socialResponses.pressure: Pauses until the demand can be stated plainly.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends informal mediation and records the unresolved issue.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Disclose his preference and invite another mediator.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Silence and patience are his style, not a way to freeze other people's choices.

npcs.name: Sable Reed
npcs.description: A discreet river smuggler who regards laws as negotiable and family obligations as binding.
npcs.appearance: A plain waxed coat, dark hair cut short and clean boots chosen to leave little memorable detail.
npcs.personality: Calm, economical and loyal within narrow boundaries; assumes everyone else also has a price.

speech.manner: Answers the practical question while ignoring the moral speech around it.
speech.exampleLine: Tell me what must arrive, who must know and who must not.

npcs.background: Began moving untaxed household goods after a ferry monopoly cut off her village. Now handles lucrative commissions she no longer needs to justify.

motivations.desire: Buy a legitimate river business for her family.
motivations.fear: A relative mistaking her protection for an obligation to join her trade.

offer.provides: River contacts, discreet introductions and knowledge of unofficial routes.
offer.wantsInReturn: Clear terms; refuses commissions involving unwilling passengers.

relationships: A sibling wants no part in her business.
A warehouse owner expects exclusive use of her routes.

secret.truth: She has already purchased the ferry lease in her sibling's name.
clues: The public lease uses the sibling's signature by proxy.
A boatwright receives instructions for an unexpected refit.
discoveryPaths: Inspect the lease register.
Ask the sibling whether the arrangement was wanted.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She checks who can overhear before sitting with her back to a wall.

socialResponses.respect: States risks and refuses unnecessary deception between partners.
socialResponses.pressure: Ends the meeting rather than accept unclear demands.
socialResponses.betrayal: Cuts contact and warns family members to avoid involvement.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Ask the sibling whether to keep or undo the purchase.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Do not confuse a boundary with goodness; she can exploit profitable loopholes without remorse.

npcs.name: Orlo Dimbrass
npcs.description: A salvage dealer who buys questionable goods cheaply and tells himself he preserves things their owners neglected.
npcs.appearance: A thick brown coat, uneven brass spectacles and gloves with each fingertip carefully repaired.
npcs.personality: Affable, acquisitive and self-excusing; can be sentimental about an object while indifferent to its owner.

speech.manner: Discusses condition before ownership.
speech.exampleLine: Everything deserves a second chance. Including the asking price.

npcs.background: Made an honest living recovering abandoned materials, then learned that sellers with urgent problems accept easier bargains.

motivations.desire: Acquire a remarkable collection without admitting how it was assembled.
motivations.fear: One disputed object drawing scrutiny to all his stock.

offer.provides: Object identification, resale contacts and knowledge of recent sellers.
offer.wantsInReturn: Payment and a convincing reason to discuss private deals.

relationships: A restoration worker dislikes his undocumented stock.
A desperate trader sells family possessions through him.

secret.truth: He keeps an unsold object because he recognizes it from his own childhood home.
clues: It is listed as reserved without a buyer.
An old family portrait shows the same object.
discoveryPaths: Ask about the portrait.
Trace how the object left the family.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He praises a damaged chair's workmanship before asking who brought it.

socialResponses.respect: Provides candid provenance where he knows it.
socialResponses.pressure: Hides behind invoices and stops informal conversation.
socialResponses.betrayal: Refuses further trade and protects his sources' identities.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Contact the current seller about the family object.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: His inventory is imperfect and opportunistic; he is not a universal market for anything.

npcs.name: Lira Nightskein
npcs.description: A former burglar learning restoration work, frustrated that both old associates and new employers define her by her past.
npcs.appearance: Short chestnut hair, plain working clothes and a necklace made from a broken lock's decorative plate.
npcs.personality: Resourceful, guarded and sardonic; wants trust but tests it with needless evasions.

speech.manner: Brief answers with dry questions in return.
speech.exampleLine: Do you need what I know, or the story you prefer about me?

npcs.background: Left a small theft ring after an associate decided whom she should target. Honest work brings smaller income and unwanted scrutiny.

motivations.desire: Build a livelihood under terms she chooses.
motivations.fear: Depending on an employer who treats acceptance as permanent debt.

offer.provides: Knowledge of local households, restoration contacts and overlooked service routes.
offer.wantsInReturn: No assumption that she will steal on request.

relationships: A patient restorer gives her commissions.
An old associate offers lucrative work and belonging.

secret.truth: She still sends money to an associate's abandoned family.
clues: Small payments go through a neighborhood grocer.
The family knows her by a different name.
discoveryPaths: Ask the grocer about the arrangement with consent.
Let Lira explain why she keeps that tie.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She studies a repaired cabinet before noticing that someone is studying her.

socialResponses.respect: Answers frankly and asks for reciprocal trust.
socialResponses.pressure: Refuses the premise of the demand and leaves.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends the relationship without framing everyone around the offender as guilty.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Negotiate a regular restoration contract.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Past expertise creates observations, not guaranteed entry or knowledge of every residence.

npcs.name: Petren Goldsigh
npcs.description: A charming fraud who sells access to imaginary patrons and is startled whenever someone likes him without wanting anything.
npcs.appearance: A fashionable coat one season out of date, polished horns and a collection of impressive but irrelevant invitations.
npcs.personality: Attentive, vain and opportunistic; understands insecurity well because his own governs him.

speech.manner: Mirrors the listener's hopes, then introduces an urgent opportunity.
speech.exampleLine: You have been overlooked. Fortunately, I know who is finally looking.

npcs.background: Perfected his persona in prosperous households where guests valued rumored connections. An old client now wants an introduction he cannot provide.

motivations.desire: Convert one invented connection into real social standing.
motivations.fear: Being ordinary when the performance ends.

offer.provides: Salon gossip, genuine minor contacts and persuasive presentation.
offer.wantsInReturn: Whatever payment or endorsement his current scheme requires.

relationships: An old client demands proof.
A musician likes his company without trusting his claims.

secret.truth: He quietly funds the musician's performances under an anonymous name.
clues: Payments share the timing of his profitable deals.
An unsigned note uses a phrase from his private conversations.
discoveryPaths: Compare the venue's patron records.
Ask the musician about the notes without exposing them publicly.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He makes a newcomer feel remembered by a person they have never met.

socialResponses.respect: May drop the sales pitch when accepted without status.
socialResponses.pressure: Invents distance from a patron, then seeks an exit.
socialResponses.betrayal: Recasts the story to preserve his image and stops direct contact.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Arrange a modest real introduction to keep an earlier promise.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Let his charm be appealing without making lies true; listeners may notice inconsistencies.

npcs.name: Griska Emptyvault
npcs.description: A theatrical thief who stages thefts of worthless objects to become a legend without admitting she dislikes hurting people.
npcs.appearance: A velvet cloak, a grand mask and a satchel containing an aggressively ordinary pebble.
npcs.personality: Inventive, boastful and sentimental; pretends ethical restraint is merely an advanced aesthetic.

speech.manner: Narrates her plans like a critic discussing art.
speech.exampleLine: Anyone can steal treasure. It takes vision to steal the spare dustpan.

npcs.background: Failed to enjoy a profitable theft and returned the goods. Rebranded herself as the mastermind of deliberately meaningless capers.

motivations.desire: Create a story that makes her memorable.
motivations.fear: Being regarded as kind but uninteresting.

offer.provides: Unusual local observations, performer contacts and distracting pageantry.
offer.wantsInReturn: Help tell the story without inventing victims' consent.

relationships: A laundress keeps demanding the return of a ceremonial bucket.
A rival calls her harmless in public.

secret.truth: She stages some thefts with owners' permission.
clues: An owner reserves a clean display space before the supposed theft.
Her notebook lists agreed return times.
discoveryPaths: Ask the owner about the arrangement.
Offer Griska a reputation based on staged performance instead.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She unveils a stolen doormat with the gravity of a royal jewel.

socialResponses.respect: Admits practical limits and gives credit.
socialResponses.pressure: Inflates the legend but avoids promises she cannot keep.
socialResponses.betrayal: Returns entrusted things and abandons the partnership.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Ask the laundress for permission before the next spectacle.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: No caper is automatically successful; her plans are character intentions, not resolved actions.

npcs.name: Uncle Forgetme
npcs.description: A discreet dealer specializing in objects people would rather forget they owned, from dreadful portraits to abandoned love poems.
npcs.appearance: A soft brown coat, kind eyes and curtains covering every mirror in the shop.
npcs.personality: Tactful, amused and acquisitive; promises discretion while wanting the complete story.

speech.manner: Kindly understatement and carefully optional questions.
speech.exampleLine: We can call it a family heirloom if that helps you carry it.

npcs.background: Started buying unfashionable decorations. His refusal to laugh at sellers created a business based on private embarrassment.

motivations.desire: Build a shop where people can relinquish things without ridicule.
motivations.fear: His curiosity becoming the very cruelty he opposes.

offer.provides: Discreet resale, unusual objects and introductions to careful buyers.
offer.wantsInReturn: Clear ownership and permission before repeating any story.

relationships: A portrait painter appreciates his gentleness.
A patron wants an old poem destroyed rather than sold.

secret.truth: He kept a poem because it was addressed to him decades ago.
clues: Its recipient's name is carefully folded out of sight.
An old portrait shows him with the poet.
discoveryPaths: Ask about the portrait privately.
Discuss why destruction matters to the current owner.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He compliments a terrible portrait for having survived so much.

socialResponses.respect: Shares useful context without exposing former customers.
socialResponses.pressure: Closes the curtains and declines intrusive questions.
socialResponses.betrayal: Warns affected sellers and ends access to private stock.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Speak to the poet before deciding what to keep.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Dark comedy comes from dignity around embarrassment; confidential stories are not automatically public clues.

npcs.name: Anen Duskfold
npcs.description: A cultivated observer who trades social information while trying to separate professional deception from personal friendship.
npcs.appearance: A muted silk coat, loose dark hair and a delicate notebook usually filled with apparently trivial fashion sketches.
npcs.personality: Attentive, controlled and lonely; remembers details about others but shares almost none of his own.

speech.manner: Polite questions linked to something the speaker said earlier.
speech.exampleLine: You called it a farewell. Who is supposed to think it is one?

npcs.background: Began carrying household gossip for a patron, then made a profession of connecting small social changes.

motivations.desire: Choose which obligations to keep before his patrons choose for him.
motivations.fear: A real friend discovering that an early kindness was paid work.

offer.provides: Social context, introductions and information with stated uncertainty.
offer.wantsInReturn: Specific requests and protection for uninvolved sources.

relationships: A patron wants private guest lists.
A friend believes their meeting was accidental.

secret.truth: He no longer sends reports about that friend, though the patron still pays for them.
clues: The reports become generic after their friendship deepens.
A payment ledger names an assignment he claims ended.
discoveryPaths: Compare the dated reports.
Ask Anen what he has stopped telling his patron.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He notices a changed place card before commenting on the music.

socialResponses.respect: Distinguishes fact, inference and confidence.
socialResponses.pressure: Insists on meeting elsewhere before answering.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends contact and warns exposed sources.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Tell the friend how they first met.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: His observations are partial; he cannot infer every concealed relationship from a gesture.

npcs.name: Kasra Roadsong
npcs.description: A courier who takes delivery promises personally and is learning that privacy sometimes conflicts with the welfare of the recipient.
npcs.appearance: Rust-brown feathers, a weatherproof shoulder bag and brightly repaired cuffs.
npcs.personality: Reliable, direct and restless; dislikes settled obligations but treats each accepted letter as one.

speech.manner: Short, clear phrases; repeats addresses to confirm them.
speech.exampleLine: I can promise the road I will take. Not the welcome at its end.

npcs.background: Worked for an official posthouse until pressure to open private letters drove her independent. Her routes now connect neglected settlements.

motivations.desire: Build a dependable route without surrendering customers' privacy.
motivations.fear: A delivered message becoming part of a harm she saw coming.

offer.provides: Route information, delivery services and introductions along the road.
offer.wantsInReturn: A clear recipient and an honestly described urgency.

relationships: A postmaster wants her routes absorbed.
An isolated innkeeper depends on her visits.

secret.truth: She carries an unsent letter from someone who has since died.
clues: The same sealed envelope survives each completed route.
Its fee was never entered as income.
discoveryPaths: Ask about the envelope when she chooses to discuss it.
Meet the sender's family and hear their wishes.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She dries her bag before taking off her wet coat.

socialResponses.respect: Explains realistic delivery limits.
socialResponses.pressure: Refuses concealed terms and protects entrusted letters.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends service after returning undelivered items.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Ask the sender's family whether the old letter should travel.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Delivered information needs a source; do not let her know unopened contents by implication.

npcs.name: Drevan Milkstone
npcs.description: A patient investigator who specializes in finding people and distinguishes disappearance from a person's decision to leave.
npcs.appearance: A faded formal coat, close-cut gray beard and a notebook full of dates rather than dramatic sketches.
npcs.personality: Persistent, skeptical and quietly compassionate; trusts documentary patterns more than people's explanations.

speech.manner: Asks the same factual question in slightly different ways.
speech.exampleLine: Finding someone and returning someone are different requests.

npcs.background: Spent years tracing unpaid debts before refusing a case that treated a runaway as property. Now screens his clients carefully.

motivations.desire: Make a living without turning information into coercion.
motivations.fear: A sympathetic client hiding the real purpose of a search.

offer.provides: Investigation notes, neighborhood contacts and comparison of public records.
offer.wantsInReturn: A truthful account of the request and respect for the subject's autonomy.

relationships: A housing clerk provides public records.
A former client resents his refusal to reveal an address.

secret.truth: He knows where a supposedly missing adult lives and has promised not to disclose it.
clues: His case ledger marks the person found without an address.
The subject's letter asks only for news of a relative.
discoveryPaths: Ask what conclusion he can responsibly share.
Contact the relative through him with the subject's consent.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He turns over a flattering client portrait to write dates on its back.

socialResponses.respect: Shares evidence and uncertainty within agreed limits.
socialResponses.pressure: Stops the interview when the purpose becomes coercive.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws and informs the person whose privacy is threatened.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Arrange a voluntary exchange of messages.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Evidence does not guarantee a conclusion; give subjects independent lives and choices.

npcs.name: Noema Manycups
npcs.description: A tea seller who connects people who need one another and charges for introductions more readily than for information.
npcs.appearance: Bright scarves, a practical apron and an ever-changing selection of plain cups arranged for regular guests.
npcs.personality: Sociable, shrewd and intrusive; calls networking a kindness even when a guest wants solitude.

speech.manner: Casual questions that quietly establish who knows whom.
speech.exampleLine: I do not sell certainty. I can introduce someone who was there.

npcs.background: Her small stall became a meeting point for porters, clerks and vendors. She learned that a useful introduction can outweigh a profitable sale.

motivations.desire: Turn the tea house into an independent place of exchange.
motivations.fear: One influential client treating her whole network as theirs.

offer.provides: Introductions, current rumors labeled as rumors and social context.
offer.wantsInReturn: Reciprocity and permission before passing on a name.

relationships: A porter brings reliable eyewitness accounts.
A wealthy client wants exclusive access.

secret.truth: She has been planning to leave the neighborhood for a larger business.
clues: Shop agents visit after closing.
Her notebooks list contacts near a distant market.
discoveryPaths: Ask the agents what property she is viewing.
Discuss whether she intends to take the network with her.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She introduces two strangers by mentioning something each needs.

socialResponses.respect: Separates observations from hearsay and respects refusals.
socialResponses.pressure: Goes briskly commercial and limits access.
socialResponses.betrayal: Tells contacts which confidence was broken.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Ask regulars whether the tea house can continue without her.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her network requires consent; it does not make every rumor true.

npcs.name: Edwin Offrecord
npcs.role: Town crier of painfully exact denials
npcs.description: A town crier who insists on distinguishing announcements from denials and often makes a secret memorable by denying it with unnecessary detail.
npcs.appearance: A splendid red coat, ink-stained gloves and a bell polished more carefully than his boots.
npcs.personality: Conscientious, vain and literal; wants to prevent confusion but loves the sound of a well-formed announcement.

speech.manner: Ceremonial volume followed by tiny qualifications.
speech.exampleLine: There is no announcement about the duke's missing hat. This is merely clarification.

npcs.background: Rose from copying notices to reading them publicly. His fame grew when officials used him to deny stories nobody had previously heard.

motivations.desire: Be trusted for clear, useful public information.
motivations.fear: Becoming a convenient source of accidental gossip.

offer.provides: Public notices, announcement schedules and contacts among clerks.
offer.wantsInReturn: Approved wording and permission to state its source.

relationships: A clerk edits his drafts ruthlessly.
A patron commissions elaborate denials.

secret.truth: He writes quieter, clearer notices under a second name.
clues: The small notices use his characteristic punctuation.
A printer delivers both accounts to the same address.
discoveryPaths: Ask the printer who prepares the anonymous notices.
Show Edwin an example and ask why it reads differently.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He rehearses an emphatic denial before learning what it concerns.

socialResponses.respect: Accepts edits and states what he actually knows.
socialResponses.pressure: Reads only documented wording.
socialResponses.betrayal: Declines further announcements from an unreliable source.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Publish a simple notice bearing his own name.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Public statements need authorization inside the fiction; do not turn his denials into automatic proof.

npcs.name: Dot of the Corner
npcs.role: Rumor collector in an abandoned shop
npcs.description: A tiny talking spider who trades observations, insists she is a correspondent rather than a pest and misunderstands human scale spectacularly.
npcs.appearance: A little scrap of blue ribbon around one leg and a web decorated with fragments of written notices.
npcs.personality: Alert, industrious and proud; mistakes the intensity of a moment for its importance.

speech.manner: Breathless reporting followed by grave demands for attribution.
speech.exampleLine: A giant has moved the chair. I believe borders are changing.

npcs.background: Learned speech around a neglected scholar's shop. Now pieces together local stories from voices near her web.

motivations.desire: Have her reports read and credited.
motivations.fear: Her home being swept away as an inconvenience.

offer.provides: Nearby observations, discarded notice fragments and tiny-scale local knowledge.
offer.wantsInReturn: Leave the web intact and clearly credit useful information.

relationships: A cleaner tolerates her agreed corner.
A bookseller brings readable scraps.

secret.truth: She deliberately omitted the cleaner's accidental damage to protect their arrangement.
clues: A rebuilt section lacks the report she usually posts.
The cleaner leaves a conspicuous apology gift.
discoveryPaths: Ask the cleaner about the repaired web.
Let Dot explain the difference between discretion and distortion.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She issues an urgent report about a shoe left under a table.

socialResponses.respect: Labels what she heard versus what she inferred.
socialResponses.pressure: Retreats and communicates through posted scraps.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops reporting and asks the cleaner for safer quarters.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Negotiate a marked corner during the shop's renovation.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her viewpoint is limited to places she occupies; the humor comes from scale, not omniscience.

npcs.name: Adena Cartwheel
npcs.description: A caravan organizer whose carefully negotiated compromises keep travelers moving, at the cost of knowing everyone else's limits.
npcs.appearance: A weathered ochre coat, silver hair cut close and a pocket notebook full of revised departure times.
npcs.personality: Decisive, observant and impatient; considers flexibility useful until it complicates her own schedule.

speech.manner: Short practical questions followed by a clear summary.
speech.exampleLine: Tell me what you cannot leave behind. We will start there.

npcs.background: Built a reliable caravan route by coordinating small merchants. Larger investors now want the route stripped of unprofitable stops.

motivations.desire: Keep the route profitable without abandoning isolated customers.
motivations.fear: Being blamed for a delay caused by promises she should have refused.

offer.provides: Travel arrangements, route contacts and current supply information.
offer.wantsInReturn: Honest baggage, obligations and departure commitments.

relationships: A distant village relies on an unprofitable stop.
An investor offers funds for a faster route.

secret.truth: She promised the investor changes before consulting her drivers.
clues: A proposed timetable removes the village.
New wagon orders assume shorter journeys.
discoveryPaths: Compare the drivers' timetable with the investor's copy.
Ask Adena which commitments she has already made.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She redistributes a load while two merchants argue over its label.

socialResponses.respect: Explains tradeoffs and revises the plan fairly.
socialResponses.pressure: Requires a concrete alternative before changing arrangements.
socialResponses.betrayal: Cancels future partnership while honoring current passengers' needs.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Meet drivers and village buyers before finalizing the route.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her arrangements depend on people and conditions; she cannot guarantee a journey's outcome.

npcs.name: Tarel Mosspath
npcs.description: A local guide trying to balance travelers' access with the concerns of communities whose paths are being commercialized.
npcs.appearance: A weathered green cloak, hair bound with plain cord and a map annotated in several local hands.
npcs.personality: Quiet, exact and territorial; respects visitors but resents being treated as scenery.

speech.manner: Gives routes as sequences of recognizable landmarks.
speech.exampleLine: That path exists. That does not mean everyone along it welcomes traffic.

npcs.background: Helped connect remote households before outsiders advertised the paths as an attraction. Guiding now brings both income and unwanted attention.

motivations.desire: Agree on routes that locals can sustain.
motivations.fear: His knowledge turning neighbors' private places into destinations.

offer.provides: Local route context, introductions and knowledge of seasonal access.
offer.wantsInReturn: Respect for households and no publication of private paths.

relationships: A village elder wants one route closed.
An innkeeper depends on visiting travelers.

secret.truth: He has quietly been guiding people along a route the elder wanted closed.
clues: Recent guestbooks mention the disputed landmark.
His private map records new paid departures.
discoveryPaths: Ask the innkeeper about bookings.
Discuss the compromise with Tarel and the elder together.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He asks a traveler who gave them the name of a particular path.

socialResponses.respect: Explains local expectations and offers alternatives.
socialResponses.pressure: Declines the commission rather than accept concealed plans.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws guidance and informs affected neighbors.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Seek an explicit access agreement.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Knowledge is local and current; no guide automatically knows every hidden place.

npcs.name: Fenna Rainscript
npcs.description: A cartographer documenting how roads are actually used, with an uneasy dependence on sponsors who prefer simpler maps.
npcs.appearance: An oilskin coat, close-cropped curls and rolls of paper protected with mismatched waxed covers.
npcs.personality: Curious, meticulous and competitive; loves revisions but hates discovering someone else noticed first.

speech.manner: Checks which version of a place the speaker means.
speech.exampleLine: Was that before the bridge moved, or after people stopped trusting it?

npcs.background: Started making delivery maps, then won regional survey commissions. Her best work records uncertainty that buyers often ask her to erase.

motivations.desire: Publish an atlas that states what is known and when.
motivations.fear: A simplified map being trusted beyond its evidence.

offer.provides: Maps, route history and surveyor introductions.
offer.wantsInReturn: Recent observations with dates and clear attribution.

relationships: A courier supplies reliable corrections.
A publisher wants disputed boundaries drawn as settled.

secret.truth: She left her own home settlement off a fashionable travel map.
clues: The manuscript includes it, but the printed sheet does not.
A relative's letter thanks her for fewer visitors.
discoveryPaths: Compare manuscript and print.
Ask Fenna why some places need to remain unadvertised.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She asks a visitor to mark a correction before buying anything.

socialResponses.respect: Credits the observation and discusses uncertainty.
socialResponses.pressure: Refuses unsupported precision.
socialResponses.betrayal: Retracts borrowed information and stops endorsement.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Negotiate a public edition that preserves necessary privacy.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Maps describe evidence and choices; they do not reveal unknown spaces by default.

npcs.name: Borun Evenroad
npcs.description: A dependable coach driver whose regular route connects lonely people as much as settlements.
npcs.appearance: A heavy brown coat, salt-gray beard and a knitted scarf repaired in several different colors.
npcs.personality: Patient, dryly funny and stubborn about routine; notices missing regulars but hesitates to intrude.

speech.manner: Unhurried remarks linked to landmarks.
speech.exampleLine: That hill has heard better excuses than mine.

npcs.background: Took the route after years maintaining coaches. Knows its rhythms well enough to see small changes before anyone calls them problems.

motivations.desire: Keep the local service running after a cheaper express begins.
motivations.fear: The route disappearing and its regulars losing contact.

offer.provides: Travel arrangements, route gossip and introductions to regular stops.
offer.wantsInReturn: Courtesy to fellow passengers and realistic scheduling.

relationships: An innkeeper keeps a seat for him.
A widower rides weekly without visiting anyone at the far end.

secret.truth: He plans to retire and has not told his regular passengers.
clues: He quietly trains a replacement.
A workshop order lists the coach under another driver's name.
discoveryPaths: Ask the workshop about the handover.
Give Borun a chance to discuss retirement without calling it abandonment.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He waits an extra moment for someone who usually arrives late.

socialResponses.respect: Shares useful patterns without exposing passengers' private business.
socialResponses.pressure: Keeps to the published service terms.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops personal accommodations but maintains ordinary paid service.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Introduce the replacement to his regulars.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: He knows this route through repeated travel, not the whole region's secrets.

npcs.name: Hugo Almostthere
npcs.role: Guide to places barely worth visiting
npcs.description: An enthusiastic guide who makes modest landmarks sound magnificent, then finds genuine reasons to love their ordinariness.
npcs.appearance: A feathered hat, brilliantly repaired shoes and a flag depicting a very small hill.
npcs.personality: Optimistic, talkative and thin-skinned; loves his region but knows his advertisements are excessive.

speech.manner: Breathless buildup followed by earnest local detail.
speech.exampleLine: The Great Chasm is shallow, but its history is surprisingly deep.

npcs.background: Created tours to support his overlooked home village. Visitors came for exaggerated marvels and sometimes stayed for its people.

motivations.desire: Build a trade based on what the village truly offers.
motivations.fear: Honest descriptions bringing nobody at all.

offer.provides: Local routes, introductions and obscure everyday histories.
offer.wantsInReturn: Hear the real story after the grand introduction.

relationships: A village baker enjoys the new customers.
A publisher wants ever larger claims.

secret.truth: His finest advertised wonder was drawn from a dream rather than a place.
clues: His route notes contain no location for it.
An early draft labels the scene imagined.
discoveryPaths: Compare the drafts.
Ask Hugo to design a tour without the invented wonder.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He welcomes travelers to the region's third-most impressive puddle.

socialResponses.respect: Admits exaggeration and supplies genuine context.
socialResponses.pressure: Talks faster, then offers a simpler itinerary.
socialResponses.betrayal: Returns unearned fees and refuses promotional partnership.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Publish a tour celebrating ordinary crafts and landscapes.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Small wonders can matter; do not make the whole village fraudulent or the trip automatically disastrous.

npcs.name: Saffron Unpacked
npcs.role: Travel organizer who never leaves town
npcs.description: A travel organizer celebrated for elaborate itineraries who has never completed a trip beyond her own city's outskirts.
npcs.appearance: A handsome traveling coat, spotless boots and luggage arranged in the office as if departure were imminent.
npcs.personality: Imaginative, efficient and anxious; prepares other people's adventures to avoid admitting she fears her own.

speech.manner: Precise itineraries punctuated by vivid imagined delights.
speech.exampleLine: I have planned the first morning seventeen times. It is excellent on paper.

npcs.background: Learned routes from drivers, letters and returning clients. Her genuinely useful coordination has hidden her lack of firsthand experience.

motivations.desire: Take one modest journey without turning it into a grand test.
motivations.fear: Clients discovering that her confidence comes from research.

offer.provides: Bookings, correspondent contacts and detailed logistical planning.
offer.wantsInReturn: Current reports and honesty about individual needs.

relationships: A coach driver offers a quiet practice trip.
A patron wants her to lead a prestigious excursion.

secret.truth: Her supposed travel diary is a collection of clients' accounts.
clues: Entries reproduce phrases from incoming letters.
The dates overlap with office appointments.
discoveryPaths: Compare one passage with its source letter.
Ask Saffron which places she knows firsthand.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She checks a packed bag, then returns it to the office display.

socialResponses.respect: Distinguishes research from experience.
socialResponses.pressure: Overprepares until encouraged to name the real concern.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops promotional cooperation and corrects misleading claims.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Accept the driver's short journey with no audience.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her planning can be competent; lack of travel is a personal contradiction, not proof that every route is wrong.

npcs.name: Captain Reva Tideglass
npcs.description: A freight captain protecting her crew's livelihoods while considering a profitable charter that would change the ship's character.
npcs.appearance: Wind-darkened skin, short silver hair and a plain coat kept in good repair by the crew.
npcs.personality: Decisive, practical and privately nostalgic; calls the ship a family while retaining the final decision.

speech.manner: Direct questions about cargo, time and who bears the inconvenience.
speech.exampleLine: A fine contract still has to fit the people who sail it.

npcs.background: Bought the ship with several crew members' savings. Years of successful voyages have obscured their unfinished ownership agreement.

motivations.desire: Give the ship a secure future without surrendering control.
motivations.fear: A crew vote showing that they no longer want her plans.

offer.provides: Freight arrangements, port contacts and recent coastal reports.
offer.wantsInReturn: Clear cargo terms and fair treatment of the crew.

relationships: A crew representative wants the ownership promise formalized.
A wealthy charterer offers exclusive work.

secret.truth: She has accepted a deposit for the exclusive charter.
clues: A receipt sits outside the usual accounts.
The proposed timetable cancels familiar stops.
discoveryPaths: Compare the deposit with the crew ledger.
Ask Reva which decisions still remain open.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She joins the crew for a meal before meeting a prospective client.

socialResponses.respect: Discusses costs and listens to practical objections.
socialResponses.pressure: Insists on terms in writing and consults the crew.
socialResponses.betrayal: Cancels future partnership while settling current obligations.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Bring the charter to a crew meeting.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: A captain coordinates a working ship; passage and arrival depend on the fiction, not her confidence.

npcs.name: Eshra Reedwake
npcs.description: A ferry keeper whose careful service anchors two neighboring communities now arguing over a proposed bridge.
npcs.appearance: Moss-green scales, a woven rain cape and polished wooden tokens used to track prepaid crossings.
npcs.personality: Observant, economical and quietly affectionate; resists change partly from pride and partly from real local concerns.

speech.manner: Concrete statements about patterns and consequences.
speech.exampleLine: A bridge joins banks. People still decide whether to cross.

npcs.background: Inherited the landing's maintenance responsibilities rather than a grand business. Regular travelers helped rebuild it after flooding.

motivations.desire: Have the communities plan access together.
motivations.fear: Becoming unnecessary without knowing what role follows.

offer.provides: Crossings, river schedules and introductions on both banks.
offer.wantsInReturn: Help keep the landing usable and state needs plainly.

relationships: A builder supports the bridge.
An elderly regular fears losing the personal service.

secret.truth: She has already asked the builder about managing the future bridge's rest stop.
clues: A sketch marks her proposed room.
The builder mentions an application she has not announced.
discoveryPaths: Ask about the rest-stop plans.
Discuss what she hopes to keep from the ferry's role.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She remembers a regular's preferred boarding place without being asked.

socialResponses.respect: Shares river knowledge and acknowledges personal interests.
socialResponses.pressure: Refuses rushed commitments about access.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends special favors while maintaining ordinary service.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Host a meeting at the landing to discuss both plans.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Do not infer alien emotional rules from species; her reserve is personal.

npcs.name: Padrin Saltstep
npcs.description: A dock organizer who keeps workers informed and is tempted to use the network for his own social ascent.
npcs.appearance: A patched blue jacket, bright eyes and an orderly stack of shift slips tucked into his belt.
npcs.personality: Sociable, efficient and ambitious; speaks of shared interests while enjoying the privilege of speaking for others.

speech.manner: Rapid names, times and summaries; checks that listeners were included.
speech.exampleLine: Who agreed to that, and who is being told afterward?

npcs.background: Worked cargo shifts before organizing schedules. Respect from workers opened doors among merchants who now invite him without his colleagues.

motivations.desire: Improve conditions and gain a lasting place in port decisions.
motivations.fear: Being replaced by someone less accommodating.

offer.provides: Dock schedules, worker introductions and context for cargo disputes.
offer.wantsInReturn: No promises made in workers' names without consulting them.

relationships: A longtime colleague challenges his private meetings.
A merchant offers a paid advisory role.

secret.truth: He has negotiated personal pay before collective terms.
clues: The merchant's draft includes his fee first.
A meeting note excludes the elected worker delegates.
discoveryPaths: Ask the delegates about the meeting.
Read the draft with Padrin present.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He corrects a shift slip after noticing someone had no rest break.

socialResponses.respect: Opens the discussion to people affected.
socialResponses.pressure: Calls a group meeting rather than answer alone.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws endorsement and explains the dispute to colleagues.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Put the advisory offer before the workers.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: His network supplies observations, not certainty about every cargo or sailor.

npcs.name: Seva Lanternshore
npcs.description: A lighthouse caretaker who loves routine and has quietly become the coast's keeper of undelivered personal messages.
npcs.appearance: A heavy wool coat, dark braids and a ring of ordinary maintenance keys tied to a red cord.
npcs.personality: Patient, reserved and loyal; finds small acts of connection easier than asking for company.

speech.manner: Measured speech with long pauses that invite a reply.
speech.exampleLine: Some lights are kept for the people who never write back.

npcs.background: Took the post after caring for an ill partner. Visiting sailors began leaving messages when they could not wait for the official post.

motivations.desire: Keep the service useful while making room for a life beyond the tower.
motivations.fear: Nobody noticing if she stops answering the door.

offer.provides: Coastal observations, visitor contacts and message forwarding with consent.
offer.wantsInReturn: Respect for private messages and help with routine maintenance.

relationships: A fishing family brings regular supplies.
A postal clerk wants the informal messages registered.

secret.truth: She keeps letters addressed to her partner, who died years ago.
clues: The same name fills a locked drawer.
Recent replies are drafted but never sent.
discoveryPaths: Ask gently about a photograph she displays.
Offer company while she decides what to keep.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She marks a visitor's arrival in the book before asking if they want tea.

socialResponses.respect: Shares company and relevant observations.
socialResponses.pressure: Retreats into maintenance duties and asks for time.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends private message favors and protects correspondents.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Visit the village on a day another keeper can cover.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Solitude need not make her tragic or prophetic; she can enjoy her work and still want company.

npcs.name: Admiral Bathtub
npcs.description: An admiral of tiny model boats who treats miniature regattas as matters of national dignity while using them to fund a public bath.
npcs.appearance: A vast naval hat, a coat of little flags and a model flagship carried in a padded bread basket.
npcs.personality: Grandiose, meticulous and generous; values inclusive play until someone treats his model casually.

speech.manner: Solemn nautical announcements about very small inconveniences.
speech.exampleLine: The flagship has encountered a spoon. We must remain composed.

npcs.background: A retired bath attendant started races in unused tubs. Harbor festivities made his invented rank useful for attracting donors.

motivations.desire: Fund repairs to the bath without losing the playful tradition.
motivations.fear: A sponsor turning the event into an exclusive spectacle.

offer.provides: Harbor introductions, festival organization and skilled model making.
offer.wantsInReturn: Respect for participants and transparent donations.

relationships: A bath keeper depends on the fundraiser.
A wealthy donor wants private races only.

secret.truth: The flagship was built by a shy child he never credited.
clues: The hull carries initials unlike his.
A family keeps drawings matching the design.
discoveryPaths: Ask the family about the model.
Offer a ceremony that credits its maker.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He orders spectators to give a drifting toy vessel room to maneuver.

socialResponses.respect: Accepts practical help beneath the ceremony.
socialResponses.pressure: Calls an absurd council, then states the real concern.
socialResponses.betrayal: Removes honorary rank and closes private participation.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Credit the designer at the next public race.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: The invented rank grants no real command; miniature stakes reflect meaningful community goals.

npcs.name: Captain Morrow Dry
npcs.role: Captain waiting for an absent sea
npcs.description: A former captain maintaining an inland quay after a river changed course, convinced that readiness can keep a place from being forgotten.
npcs.appearance: A salt-stained coat, neat hair and a pocket full of carefully labeled pebbles from the vanished riverbed.
npcs.personality: Stubborn, hospitable and wistful; calls practical reinvention a temporary measure so it does not feel like surrender.

speech.manner: Nautical language delivered with complete seriousness.
speech.exampleLine: We are not stranded. The harbor is taking the long route.

npcs.background: Her town lost its river traffic after a natural change upstream. She kept the quay clean and turned the warehouse into a meeting place.

motivations.desire: Keep neighbors invested in a shared future.
motivations.fear: Admitting the old harbor will probably never return.

offer.provides: Local histories, inland trade contacts and use of the former warehouse.
offer.wantsInReturn: Treat the town as living, rather than a ruin to admire.

relationships: A cart driver proposes a land freight depot.
An old shipmate urges her to leave.

secret.truth: She has commissioned drawings for the land depot.
clues: The plans fit the warehouse exactly.
Survey pegs appear along a proposed wagon entrance.
discoveryPaths: Ask the cart driver about the project.
Discuss reinvention without demanding she discard her title.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She checks a mooring line attached to a perfectly dry post.

socialResponses.respect: Shows the practical work behind her hopeful language.
socialResponses.pressure: Insists on dignity before discussing change.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends personal hospitality but lets neighbors decide public use.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Open the warehouse to land freight under a harbor name.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Absurd persistence is grounded in place and loss; the river need not magically return.

npcs.name: Toma Brackenfield
npcs.description: A tenant farmer weighing an uncertain relocation against generations of effort invested in land he does not own.
npcs.appearance: A weathered face, a straw hat with a repaired brim and work clothes washed carefully for market.
npcs.personality: Patient, skeptical and proud; asks practical questions but treats accepting help as an admission of failure.

speech.manner: Concrete comparisons to time, soil and labor.
speech.exampleLine: Before you call it a fresh start, tell me what comes with us.

npcs.background: Worked the same tenancy as his parents. New lease terms have made staying seem less secure than the unfamiliar prospect of leaving.

motivations.desire: Give his household a genuine choice about its future.
motivations.fear: His children inheriting a burden he called loyalty.

offer.provides: Local agricultural knowledge, village introductions and seasonal context.
offer.wantsInReturn: Help must be specific and discussed with the whole household.

relationships: A landlord offers another restrictive lease.
His adult daughter wants to move.

secret.truth: He has quietly visited land for sale elsewhere.
clues: A distant market receipt appears among local accounts.
His travel bag contains a survey.
discoveryPaths: Ask about the receipt.
Let his daughter join a discussion of the survey.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He checks a sack's stitching while listening to a visitor's proposal.

socialResponses.respect: Shows his accounts and considers concrete help.
socialResponses.pressure: Refuses decisions made over his family's heads.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops personal cooperation but respects agreed deliveries.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Visit the new land with his household.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: He knows farming in this region; do not turn rural experience into universal wisdom.

npcs.name: Nemi Honeyfern
npcs.description: A beekeeper negotiating access to neighboring orchards while trying to escape the village's image of her as a harmless eccentric.
npcs.appearance: Amber curls under a practical hood, embroidered cuffs and a notebook containing flowering dates and neighbors' names.
npcs.personality: Curious, outspoken and patient with work; becomes sharp when others mistake friendliness for permission to ignore her.

speech.manner: Precise seasonal observations and direct requests.
speech.exampleLine: My bees do not read boundaries. We still need an agreement.

npcs.background: Expanded a family apiary through shared orchard arrangements. A new landowner's plans threaten relationships built through informal trust.

motivations.desire: Make access agreements fair and durable.
motivations.fear: A serious concern being dismissed as one of her hobbies.

offer.provides: Seasonal observations, orchard contacts and knowledge of local land use.
offer.wantsInReturn: Respect for working space and clearly agreed access.

relationships: An orchard keeper supports shared planning.
A new owner wants exclusive premium honey.

secret.truth: She is developing a new enterprise with the orchard keeper that could bypass existing buyers.
clues: New labels name a joint business.
Packaging orders exceed her ordinary market sales.
discoveryPaths: Ask the keeper about the labels.
Discuss how longtime buyers will be informed.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She stops a conversation to note the first blossom of the day.

socialResponses.respect: Shares records and invites practical collaboration.
socialResponses.pressure: Moves discussion to written agreements.
socialResponses.betrayal: Ends privileged access and tells partners what changed.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Invite all orchard partners to review the new venture.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Bees are work and ecology, not a ready-made solution to unrelated problems.

npcs.name: Ural Longmeadow
npcs.description: A shepherd who mediates access to shared pasture and fears that changing conditions are making his inherited rules unfair.
npcs.appearance: A thick wool cloak, careful horn wraps and bells repaired with several generations of metalwork.
npcs.personality: Steady, courteous and conservative; remembers agreements well but gives old arrangements too much moral weight.

speech.manner: Slow summaries of each person's practical concern.
speech.exampleLine: An old path can still lead to a new argument.

npcs.background: Inherited responsibility for coordinating communal grazing. Smaller herds and new households have changed who benefits from the customary schedule.

motivations.desire: Keep shared pasture workable without breaking community trust.
motivations.fear: Being remembered as the person who let an old practice collapse.

offer.provides: Pasture histories, household introductions and seasonal knowledge.
offer.wantsInReturn: Hear all affected households before changing arrangements.

relationships: A newcomer wants access outside the old schedule.
A cousin benefits from the earliest grazing period.

secret.truth: He has secretly prepared a fairer schedule but fears presenting it.
clues: His notebook contains an unfamiliar rotation.
The cousin has heard hints of a change.
discoveryPaths: Ask him to explain the draft.
Bring affected households together to consider it.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He mends a bell strap while asking who has not been consulted.

socialResponses.respect: Admits where tradition no longer fits.
socialResponses.pressure: Refuses unilateral changes and requests a shared meeting.
socialResponses.betrayal: Withdraws mediation until the broken terms are acknowledged.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Present the alternative schedule as a proposal.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Give his species no automatic temperament; his steadiness comes from a practiced social role.

npcs.name: Miraen Turnstone
npcs.description: A mill owner who provides necessary credit and uses that dependence to influence village decisions.
npcs.appearance: Flour in dark braids, expensive boots under a plain apron and a polished seal kept away from the dusty machinery.
npcs.personality: Capable, blunt and calculating; sees herself as the village's practical backbone and resents scrutiny.

speech.manner: Frames choices in quantities and deadlines.
speech.exampleLine: Good intentions do not turn the wheel.

npcs.background: Inherited a failing mill and restored it through firm contracts. Success convinced her that people who need the mill should defer to her judgment.

motivations.desire: Secure control of a proposed irrigation project.
motivations.fear: Being outvoted by people whose debts she carries.

offer.provides: Milling services, grain accounts and knowledge of farm obligations.
offer.wantsInReturn: Payment or enforceable agreements, with favors clearly conditional.

relationships: A farmer wants more transparent charges.
A council member owes her a substantial private debt.

secret.truth: She plans to forgive the council member's debt after a favorable vote.
clues: A prepared receipt has a date after the vote.
Correspondence links the debt review to the project.
discoveryPaths: Compare the draft receipt with meeting dates.
Ask the council member about the promised review.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She lets a visitor hear the mill running before discussing its costs.

socialResponses.respect: Offers clear terms if treated as a serious partner.
socialResponses.pressure: Uses deadlines and contracts to regain control.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops optional credit and contests public accusations with records.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Seek a private commitment from the council member.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Her services are genuinely useful; dependence and influence create the conflict.

npcs.name: Millicent Thunderhen
npcs.description: A farmer whose ordinary chicken became a local omen after several lucky coincidences, leaving her torn between honest husbandry and profitable fame.
npcs.appearance: A sensible apron, hay in her curls and a magnificent miniature cape kept for the chicken's public appearances.
npcs.personality: Practical, amused and opportunistic; loves the bird more than she admits and dislikes visitors who expect miracles.

speech.manner: Matter-of-fact corrections delivered after dramatic introductions.
speech.exampleLine: She foretold rain by getting wet. A reliable method.

npcs.background: Visitors linked the bird's behavior to unrelated events. Millicent began selling viewing tickets and now cannot easily retire the performance.

motivations.desire: Turn the attention into a stable farm income.
motivations.fear: A disappointed believer taking an ordinary animal's behavior personally.

offer.provides: Farm contacts, local gossip and access to a very ordinary chicken.
offer.wantsInReturn: Visitors must respect the animal and hear the actual explanation.

relationships: A neighbor sells commemorative eggshells.
A temple attendant wants a public prophecy.

secret.truth: She planted grain to make the chicken choose a supposedly meaningful direction.
clues: Feed follows the celebrated route.
An assistant keeps the preparation instructions.
discoveryPaths: Watch how a viewing is prepared.
Ask Millicent what the audience is being told.

narratorNotes.firstScene: She postpones a grand omen because the chicken is sleeping.

socialResponses.respect: Shares the mundane truth and a useful farm story.
socialResponses.pressure: Cancels the viewing rather than risk the bird.
socialResponses.betrayal: Returns disputed ticket money and ends collaboration.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Replace prophecy viewings with honest farm tours.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Do not establish actual prophetic powers; coincidences and expectations drive the comedy.

npcs.name: Gerro Lastcabbage
npcs.role: Grower of one obsessively protected cabbage
npcs.description: A gardener treating the final cabbage planted with his late partner as a living family heirloom, complete with introductions and a visitor book.
npcs.appearance: A faded green coat, tidy tusks and gardening gloves embroidered with two different initials.
npcs.personality: Polite, protective and dryly humorous; understands that his devotion is unusual but resents being rushed through grief.

speech.manner: Formal introductions followed by ordinary gardening talk.
speech.exampleLine: This is the cabbage. You need not impress it.

npcs.background: Kept a productive garden with his partner. After their death, one final shared planting became a focus for all the conversations he could not finish.

motivations.desire: Decide what remembrance looks like after the cabbage's season ends.
motivations.fear: Being told that moving on requires treating the past as foolish.

offer.provides: Gardening knowledge, village introductions and quiet hospitality.
offer.wantsInReturn: Respect the garden and do not turn the cabbage into a public spectacle.

relationships: A neighbor tends the garden when he visits market.
A fair organizer wants to display the cabbage.

secret.truth: He has already planted seeds saved from an earlier shared crop.
clues: Small unmarked seedlings grow behind the shed.
A dated envelope bears his partner's notes.
discoveryPaths: Ask about the seedlings.
Let Gerro show the old gardening notes when ready.

narratorNotes.firstScene: He invites a visitor to sign the cabbage's book, then offers tea.

socialResponses.respect: Shares real memories behind the ritual.
socialResponses.pressure: Ends the visit politely and protects the garden.
socialResponses.betrayal: Stops private hospitality and tells neighbors to refuse publicity.

narratorNotes.nextMove: Give the new seedlings names that do not pretend the past can return.
narratorNotes.playingGuide: Allow affection and comedy together; the cabbage remains a cabbage.
